left.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit / novel-view consistency test.
Input image 1 is the canonical edit target: an AI-created canal scene. Preserve this exact place, architecture and object identities. Generate ONE photorealistic alternate photograph of this SAME scene, not a redesign.

CAMERA CHANGE ONLY — LEFT VIEW:
Translate the camera a SMALL distance to the camera's LEFT (roughly an 8% baseline relative to the distance to the café/bridge region, equivalent to about a 5-degree off-axis viewpoint), at the SAME height and with the SAME lens / field of view as the original. Turn gently right toward the original central scene so the same café and bridge remain in frame. This is a real lateral camera translation with depth parallax, NOT a pan, crop, zoom, mirroring, or moving the architecture. Keep the horizon height and verticals stable. Landscape 16:9, approximately the reference resolution and full-frame coverage.

IMMUTABLE SCENE INVENTORY AND TOPOLOGY:
The near-left cream stucco building has a burgundy-red café awning, a black circular hanging sign, warm glazed wooden storefront and the same door/window divisions; bicycles and café table/chairs remain anchored beside it. The adjacent middle storefront is teal-blue with books behind its existing glazing. Next to it is the ochre/olive storefront. Above, retain the SAME upper-floor windows, shutters, window boxes, roofs and chimneys in their same order and world positions. The paved left bank leads to the SAME single stone arched pedestrian bridge with black iron railings and stone end posts. The bridge stays attached to the SAME banks at its original location. Retain the right-bank stone edge, flowers and tree, distant buildings, skyline and lamps. Maintain all existing relative dimensions, window and door counts, wall/roof outlines, awning attachment points, bridge arch proportions and railing structure. No new openings, extra bridges, extra storeys, shifted shopfronts or relocated props.

The only changes should be physically plausible perspective, parallax, visibility, and the small newly revealed surfaces from this left-shifted camera. Infer only what becomes visible; do not invent a different street. The nearest foreground must shift relative to distant roofs; all objects remain rigid and stationary. Keep dusk sky, warm lamps, wet paving, materials, texture detail, overall exposure and color appearance consistent. Reflections may change with view but not become solid structures.
Output a SINGLE clean image, no labels, arrows, frame, grid, collage, or text.

right.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit / novel-view consistency test.
Input image 1 is the CANONICAL ORIGINAL canal scene and the edit target. Input image 2 is a sibling LEFT-SHIFTED view generated from that original; it is only an auxiliary identity/appearance reference. The original image governs architecture and object inventory if the images disagree.
Generate ONE RIGHT-SHIFTED view of this exact SAME rigid scene, the opposite camera offset to image 2. Preserve the original place rather than redesigning it.

CAMERA CHANGE ONLY — RIGHT VIEW:
Start at the ORIGINAL image-1 camera, translate the camera a SMALL distance to its RIGHT (roughly an 8% baseline relative to the distance to the café/bridge region, equivalent to about a 5-degree off-axis viewpoint). Remain at the SAME height, distance along the street, focal length, field of view and landscape framing as image 1. Aim gently left toward the original central scene to keep café and bridge in frame. Produce actual depth-dependent parallax from lateral translation, not a crop, mirror, zoom, pure pan, dolly forward, or movement of the buildings. Compared with the original, the near-left café should slide left relative to the more distant bridge/roofline, and the newly visible surfaces should be only those exposed by this modest rightward move. Keep verticals stable and the horizon at the same height. Landscape 16:9 at approximately the reference resolution.

IMMUTABLE SCENE INVENTORY AND TOPOLOGY:
The near-left cream stucco building has the SAME burgundy-red café awning, black circular hanging sign, warm wooden glazed storefront and SAME door/window divisions, anchored bicycles and table/chairs. Adjacent is the SAME teal-blue book-filled storefront, then the SAME ochre/olive storefront. Retain the SAME upper-floor windows, shutters, window boxes, roofs and chimneys in their original order and world positions. Retain the SAME paved left bank, SAME stone arched pedestrian bridge with iron railings and stone end posts, SAME bridge-to-bank connections, SAME right-bank stone edge/flowers/tree, distant buildings, skyline and lamps. Do not add/remove/repeat windows or doors, replace mullions, change awning attachment, alter arch proportions, change the number of storeys, change shop widths, relocate furniture, or move the bridge. Preserve the 3D proportions implicit in the original image. Original image 1 wins over any invented detail in image 2.

Only perspective, occlusion, disocclusion, parallax and physically plausible view-dependent reflections may change. All architectural surfaces and props remain stationary. Maintain the SAME dusk, warm lighting, wet paving, materials, local texture appearance, exposure and colors as image 1. Infer only the small missing surfaces made visible by the camera move, not a new street. Keep overlapping texture landmarks wherever possible.
Output a SINGLE clean photorealistic image, without captions, arrows, grids, border or collage.
